top_story: Netanyahu’s 9 August public rejection of a US-backed 15-point Gaza plan marked a sharp break with Washington and locked Israeli policy to an open-ended military presence until Hamas is disarmed. Hours later, an Israeli general’s call to keep Gaza “destroyed for generations” and under permanent control reinforced that rejectionist line, signaling that parts of Israel’s security establishment are framing devastation and despair as instruments of rule rather than temporary wartime costs. Those statements followed 8 August attacks across Gaza and the West Bank in which Israeli forces and settlers killed three Palestinians, wounded dozens, and targeted homes, property, and a mosque, underscoring that coercion is shaping daily life beyond formal battlefield lines. The immediate trajectory is a widening gap between diplomatic pressure for de-escalation and Israeli positions that normalize prolonged destruction, raising the likelihood of deeper Palestinian displacement, trauma, and regional political strain.
